name: Primo Brands Corporation
business: Primo Brands sells branded bottled and spring water (Poland Spring, Saratoga, Primo) through retailers and direct home and office water delivery in North America.

events.from: Primo Brands board member (listed as director in the S-1, doc 101757); ex Chairman and CEO of Aramark and Pepsi Bottling Group per board bio

events.what: COO role eliminated, Robert Austin out (support through 2026-12-31); new President of Customer Direct and Go-to-Market added, supply chain chief reports to CEO

events.from: Planet Fitness CFO; ex Keurig Dr Pepper CFO

events.who: Kimberly Reed; Minsok Pak; Allison Spector

events.what: Primo Water and BlueTriton merger closed November 2024, outside the 18-month window; it is context for the synergy target, not a scored catalyst
events.from: Primo Water Corporation and BlueTriton Brands

next_event.source: CFO David Hass: 'we would say for our traditional sort of guidance reveal on 2027 in the spring of next year' (Q2 2026 call, 2026-08-05, doc 129714); Foss: 'As we go forward into 2027, we will provide more specifics' (Barclays conference, 2026-09-09, doc 219517). Q3 2026 results date not in Baba. Rietbroek's move to GPK is the Stage 2 claim and was not verified in Baba.

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Two numeric targets, both set under the prior CEO: 25% adjusted EBITDA margin by 2027 (from the February 2025 Investor Day, which is not in Baba; restated by CEO Rietbroek and CFO Hass in August 2025) and $300M run-rate cost synergies captured by year-end 2026 (CFO Hass, 2025-02-20). Foss kept the synergy target ('We are not changing our synergy capture targets', 2025-11-06) but has not restated 25%. He describes the targets as inherited and under review, with 2027 specifics due in spring 2027. FY2026 guide is 21.8% at the midpoint, flat on 2025.

street.gap_assumption: 25% adjusted EBITDA margin target for 2027 vs VA FY-2027 consensus EBITDA 1,605.1M on revenue 7,082.3M = 22.66% (VA labels equal calendar years, fyem 12); VA EBITDA and company adjusted EBITDA are treated as the same basis (FY2026 consensus 21.67% vs company guide midpoint 21.8%). Even FY2028 consensus (23.11%) sits 189 bps below 25%. The target predates the CEO change and is under review, so the gap may close by the target being cut rather than by margins rising. pctile_ev_ebitda_60m is null in data_comps (only 27 months of history since the merger); data_financials puts NTM EV/EBITDA at the 7th percentile of that short history (7.43x vs 6.72x to 11.01x). LTM margin is Q2 2025 to Q1 2026 VA quarters (Q2 2026 actuals not yet loaded).

evidence_of_progress.note: Comparable adjusted EBITDA margin: Q1 2026 18.8%, down 260 bps (Hass, doc 189930; VA basis -234 bps); Q2 2026 21.4%, up 10 bps and up 260 bps sequentially (Hass, doc 129714). Direct delivery returned to growth (+0.4%) in Q2 2026. Net leverage 3.42x vs a target below 3x; no covenant stress seen. PET and diesel costs matter (diesel hedged into 2027) but margin is not commodity-price driven.

verdict: Highest mechanical score of the four, but the 234 bps gap is to an inherited 2027 target the board-insider CEO is reviewing, so a spring 2027 reset is as likely as a re-rating.
open_questions: Will Foss reaffirm, push out or cut the 25% 2027 margin target at the spring 2027 guidance? That decides whether the gap is opportunity or reset risk.
How much of the $300M synergy is already in the 21.8% FY2026 guide, and what is left for 2027?
Is the A score robust? data_comps has no 60-month EV/EBITDA percentile (27 months of post-merger history), so A=2 rests on the short-history 7th percentile.
